There will be positive economic aspects in this area also. Restoration of some endangered species will involve elimination of sources of pollution, thus providing enhanced water quality. Aquatic habitats now of little value for recreational use will come to support a variety of water-related recreational and sporting activities, for clean up efforts will favor game fish and their food species as well as the endangered species. The aesthetic values of a clear-running stream over a polluted stream are difficult to relate directly in economic terms but are nontheless important to the development of any water-related recreational industry.
When in conflict with the welfare of an endangered species, clearing the land of trees and woody vegetation may have to be stopped or curtailed. Such clearing may be for the production of saw timber or other forest products or for the creation of pasture for grazing or open lands for the production of agricultural crops. Economic impacts will occur in the value of timber not harvested, grazing foregone or which may have to take place at a less profitable site as well as farm products which may have to be produced elsewhere. Clearing for grazing and farming is at least partially responsible for the predicament of half the endangered Hawaiian land bird species. A number of birds characteristic of the grasslands including the prairie chickens and cranes have lost vast acreages of habitat to the plow and cow. Agriculture is competing for the remaining few acres of Columbian whitetailed deer habitat on the Columbia River between Washington and Oregon. Some species are threatened by silviculture practices considered by foresters to be efficient forest management measures.
